features.name: CLI skeleton and config loader
features.behavior: `ai-codebase-auditor audit <repo-path>` checks that the path exists and is a git working tree, loads and validates the factor configuration from config/factors.json (or --config <file>), and prints the target and a summary of the loaded factors. Invalid arguments, a bad path or an invalid config exit with code 2 and a message naming each problem. No collectors run yet, and nothing is written to the target.
features.verification: Unit tests cover argument parsing, target validation and every config validation error. The e2e smoke run audits a temporary git repository with the default config, and with a broken config file.

features.name: Git-history collector
features.behavior: Reads the target's history with read-only git commands and returns per-file signals with evidence: commit count over the full history and the last 12 months, distinct authors, and first and last commit dates, plus repository totals. A missing git binary or a shallow clone is reported as not measurable, never guessed.
features.verification: Unit tests run the collector against temporary fixture repositories with known commits, authors and dates, including a shallow clone. No test touches a real clone.

features.name: Scoring engine
features.behavior: Turns collector signals into a 1 to 5 score per factor using thresholds in config/factors.json; each score lists its evidence. A factor without evidence gets no score and is reported as not measured. A documented, dated deferral raises a score by one level. The lowest blocking factor sets the readiness level, and scores are never averaged.
features.verification: Table-driven unit tests cover every threshold edge, the deferral rule, missing evidence and the lowest-blocking-factor rule.

features.name: Decision engine
features.behavior: Maps the factor profile to one verdict: adopt when no blocking factor is weak, adapt when specific factors fail but modules are individually workable, prepare first when tests and boundaries are both missing. Assigns each module a risk zone (green, yellow, red). Every verdict names the rule and the factor scores that triggered it.
features.verification: Unit tests cover each verdict rule, its boundaries and risk-zone assignment, including red zones for auth, billing and permission paths.

features.name: Hotspots in risk zones
features.behavior: Uses the git-history and code-structure signals already collected to mark hotspot files in green modules: product source files whose commits in the last 12 months and whose length are both at or above the module's configured percentile and configured minimums. A hotspot with no test file named after it is listed as a yellow path inside its green module (characterization tests before agents edit that file), citing its commit count, length and the missing test; the module itself stays green, as it does around red paths. Thresholds live in config/decision.json. Factor scores and the verdict do not change.
features.verification: Unit tests cover the hotspot rule at each threshold edge, test-name matching, history that is not measured, and yellow paths inside green modules with scores and the verdict unchanged. The five calibration repositories are re-audited and every untested hotspot is checked against the clone.

features.name: Read-only MCP server over a saved report
features.behavior: `ai-codebase-auditor mcp <report.json>` starts a stdio MCP server that answers from a saved JSON report only: the verdict and its rule, one factor's score and evidence, the zone of a given path with its reason (red paths win over their module), the red paths, and the roadmap. It never re-audits, reads the audited repository or runs anything, and it refuses a report whose schemaVersion it does not support. A skill file in templates/ tells agents to ask for a path's zone before editing it.
features.verification: Unit tests call every tool against a fixture report, including a red path inside a green module, an unknown path and an unsupported schemaVersion. An e2e test starts the built server, lists its tools and calls each one over stdio.

features.name: SARIF output and a verdict gate for CI
features.behavior: With --out, the audit also writes ai-readiness-report.sarif (SARIF 2.1.0): one result per weak factor, yellow module and red path, each with its rule id, level, location and the evidence text from the JSON report. `--fail-on <adapt|prepare-first>` exits with code 1 when the verdict is at or below that level, and a provisional verdict is reported as such. Without --fail-on, exit codes are unchanged. Output stays deterministic.
features.verification: Unit tests validate the SARIF output against the 2.1.0 schema for the calibration-like fixtures and cover each --fail-on level, the provisional case and invalid values (exit code 2). The e2e smoke test checks the exit codes of the built CLI.

features.name: Installable package and GitHub Action
features.behavior: `npm pack` produces a package that installs and runs with `npx ai-codebase-auditor audit <repo>` on Node.js 18 or newer, holding only dist/, config/, templates the product needs, README.md and LICENSE. A composite GitHub Action (action.yml) runs the audit on the checked-out repository, uploads the SARIF report to code scanning, attaches the Markdown report as the job summary, and passes --fail-on through. Publishing to npm or the Marketplace stays a human step.
features.verification: An e2e test packs the tarball, installs it into a temporary directory and audits a fixture repository with the installed binary, and checks the tarball's file list. The Action is run in this repository's CI against a fixture repository.

features.name: Compare two audits
features.behavior: `ai-codebase-auditor compare <before.json> <after.json>` reports what changed between two saved reports of the same repository: the verdict, each factor's score and reason, zone changes per module, red paths added or removed, and roadmap steps completed, with both audited commits. Reports of different repositories or unsupported schemaVersions are refused with exit code 2. With --out, writes the comparison as Markdown and JSON.
features.verification: Unit tests compare fixture reports with no change, a raised and a lowered score, a verdict change, zone moves, a different repository and mismatched schema versions. The e2e test audits a fixture repository at two commits and compares the results.

features.name: Portfolio audit of many repositories
features.behavior: `ai-codebase-auditor audit-batch <list-file> --out <dir>` audits each repository path in the list into its own subfolder, so one failing repository is reported with its error and never stops the rest. It writes a portfolio summary in Markdown and JSON: each repository's verdict, readiness level, weak factors and red-path count, sorted by verdict, plus counts per verdict. The same safety rules as a single audit apply to every repository.
features.verification: Unit tests cover list parsing, a missing path, a non-git directory and a repository whose audit throws, beside healthy ones. The e2e test runs a batch of fixture repositories, one of them broken, and checks the summary and the per-repository reports.

features.name: Agreement between zones and recorded agent outcomes
features.behavior: `ai-codebase-auditor validate <report.json> <outcomes.json>` reads agent task outcomes recorded by a separate runner (task id, files changed, passed or failed, model and harness used) in a documented schema, and reports success counts and rates with confidence intervals per zone and per verdict, whether green ≥ yellow ≥ red holds, and which tasks touched red paths. The auditor never runs agents or the audited code; with too few tasks per zone it says so instead of reporting a rate.
features.verification: Unit tests cover the outcomes schema, a file that names paths missing from the report, ordered and unordered results, and zones with too few tasks. The e2e test validates a fixture outcomes file against a fixture report.
